_note: Caption and alt text for every image and video in media/. The five recordings (sdk-quickstart, sdk-events, sdk-admitted-executed-sealed, sdk-compile, sdk-remote) are real terminal output of the published @supernovae-st/nika 0.124.0 and the engine it bundles, nika 0.124.0 (866ed914b), rendered by scripts/media/render.mjs; every model call in them is mock/echo, the engine's offline rehearsal model. sdk-doors is an illustration whose content was captured from the same release; media/README.md says what is captured and what is drawn.

media/gifs/sdk-admitted-executed-sealed..caption: Three facts in order. Admitted: check() refuses list-files.nika (NIKA-SEC-004, with its fix) and run() never starts it, so no run, events or trace exist; one permits line makes it run. Executed is not sealed: on a machine with no signing key the run succeeds with sealed false and traceVerify() answers receipt_mismatch; after the quick start's NIKA_KEYCHAIN=off nika key init the next run of the same file is sealed and verified. Then one changed byte in the trace, and the stored receipt no longer verifies: the engine answers BROKEN at line 5. Recorded from @supernovae-st/nika 0.124.0 and its bundled engine; the runs are mock/echo rehearsals.
media/gifs/sdk-admitted-executed-sealed..alt: cat list-files.nika shows a workflow that runs ls -1 under permits: {}. node gate.mts list-files.nika prints check refused · exit 2, NIKA-SEC-004 and its fix (add ls to permits.exec), then run not started · NIKA-SEC-004 · no run, no events, no trace. A diff adds exec: [ls] to the permits, and the fixed file checks clean (exit 0) and runs. node prove.mts on a machine with no signing key: run succeeded, receipt sealed false · 5 events, verify not verified · invalid · receipt_mismatch. NIKA_KEYCHAIN=off ./node_modules/.bin/nika key init mints a key, and node prove.mts prints receipt sealed true · 6 events and verify verified. node tamper.mts changes one byte on line 4 of the trace, and node verify.mts, from the stored receipt, prints not verified · invalid and engine BROKEN at line 5.

media/gifs/sdk-compile.gif.caption: compile() turns one sentence into a checked workflow candidate and runs nothing. No provider is seated, so no model is called: round 1 is incomplete, with one required question (the runtime model) and four optional ones, and records every morning as a trigger, not a task; answering model = mock/echo makes round 2 ready with no provider call, and the schedule still requires binding. The candidate asks to read ./inbox/**, write ./digest.md and call five nika: tools, and nika check plans it in 9 waves. Recorded from @supernovae-st/nika 0.124.0 and its bundled engine; the candidate is never run.
media/gifs/sdk-compile.gif.alt: node author.mts with the intent Every morning, summarize ./inbox/*.md into ./digest.md prints round 1 incomplete · 1 required, 4 optional question(s), the required question model (which explicit runtime provider/model should run the language steps), and every morning is a trigger, not a task; answer model = mock/echo; round 2 ready · provider calls: none; trigger schedule · daily · requires_binding; check clean · exit 0 · kept as digest.nika. The next screen shows the permits block of digest.nika: fs read ./inbox/**, fs write ./digest.md, and the tools nika:assert, nika:glob, nika:jq, nika:read and nika:write. The last screen shows nika check digest.nika: 9 waves, 9 tasks, from glob_source to write_output.

media/gifs/sdk-remote.gif.caption: The same Nika class over HTTP. The README's server setup, typed as written: a one-line nika.yaml, a 0600 token file that is never printed, .nika/ kept out of git, a signing key, and nika serve on loopback, sent to the background of the same terminal. Then a client built with new Nika({ url, token, allowInsecureHttp: true }) lists and checks the served hello.nika, runs it with an idempotency key, receives two sequenced events, reads verified · sealed from the server, gets the same job back for the same key, and a typed 401 for a wrong token. Recorded from @supernovae-st/nika 0.124.0 and nika serve 0.124.0; the run is a mock/echo rehearsal.
media/gifs/sdk-remote.gif.alt: The terminal creates a one-line nika.yaml, mints a token into .nika/serve.token with umask 077 and openssl, appends .nika/ to .gitignore, runs NIKA_KEYCHAIN=off ./node_modules/.bin/nika key init, and starts ./node_modules/.bin/nika serve --bind 127.0.0.1:8787 --workflows . --token-file .nika/serve.token in the background; curl /health returns engineVersion 0.124.0 and machineProtocolVersion 2. node remote.mts prints served hello.nika, check clean, a job id, #1 run.started running, #2 run.settled succeeded, result succeeded · mock(echo) · Say hello from the Nika SDK., verify verified · sealed (the server's verdict on its own journal), retry the same job: it did not run twice, and bad token 401 unauthorized. kill %1 stops the server.

media/gifs/sdk-doors.gif.caption: An illustration of how the TypeScript SDK runs a workflow. new Nika() starts the bundled engine as a child process and new Nika({ url, token }) reaches nika serve with the same methods and other options: line 3 of the README's demo.mts takes url, token and allowInsecureHttp, and line 6 takes an idempotencyKey in place of maxCostUsd, which a server run refuses. The engine refuses list-files.nika (NIKA-SEC-004) before any run exists, runs hello.nika, streams six local events or two server events, seals six hash-chained journal lines and verifies the receipt; one changed byte makes the verifier report BROKEN at line 5. The code is the README's quick start, which the capture ran, and its lines 3 and 6 as the capture's remote driver ran them; every event, verdict, hash and version on screen was captured from @supernovae-st/nika 0.124.0, its bundled engine 0.124.0 (866ed914b) and nika serve 0.124.0 in a mock/echo rehearsal. The cards, lanes, packets and pacing are drawn, and a real run takes milliseconds. The GIF is 960 px wide; the MP4 is 1600 px, with readable code.
media/gifs/sdk-doors.gif.alt: Animated diagram. On the left is the README's demo.mts, with a panel of what the app reads. In the middle, the @supernovae-st/nika package is a column with one junction. On the right are two doors: new Nika() leads to the bundled engine nika 0.124.0, run as a child process, and new Nika({ url, token }) leads to nika serve. Lines 3 and 6 are edited to the server door's options and back: line 3's cwd: process.cwd() becomes url, token, allowInsecureHttp: true, and line 6's maxCostUsd: 0 becomes idempotencyKey. A refused list-files.nika gets NIKA-SEC-004, and run() throws NikaOperationError with no run. hello.nika is run ready. Six local events and two server events land in the app's panel. The engine's six hash-chained journal lines end with run_sealed. The receipt goes back for traceVerify(): verified locally and sealed by the server. One changed byte makes the verifier report BROKEN at line 5.

media/stills/sdk-doors.png.alt: A dark diagram titled Your app asks. The engine decides. The receipt proves it. On the left, demo.mts from the README quick start, line 6 wrapped onto a second row that holds maxCostUsd: 0, and a panel of what the app reads: six local events from run.started to run.settled succeeded, two remote events #1 run.started and #2 run.settled, and the greeting mock(echo) · Say hello from the Nika SDK. On the right, new Nika() leads to nika 0.124.0 (866ed914b) as a child process: hello.nika run ready, list-files.nika NIKA-SEC-004, the greeting task, six hash-chained journal lines ending in run_sealed, and the receipt verified. Below, new Nika({ url, token }) leads to nika serve 0.124.0: check clean, a durable job with the same idempotency key, and the server's verdict sealed.
